shipit.what: Routes a task to the playbook for its kind, runs it with subagents and the other skills, and stops only when there is proof.
shipit.use: Any real task: a bug, a feature, a PR to land, a question about the code.
shipit.skip: You already know the one skill you want. Type that one.
shipit.prompt: /shipit the csv export drops its last row. repro first, then fix and verify.
shipit.get: The work, a proof pack sized to the change, and a cost receipt when subagents ran.

setup-shipit.what: Picks the model per role and the effort budget, and detects codex and berth.
setup-shipit.use: First install, or when you want to trade cost against quality.

shipit-help.what: Tells you which skill or playbook fits, and hands you a prompt to send.
shipit-help.use: You're not sure what to use.
shipit-help.prompt: /shipit-help which skill should I use to review this branch?
shipit-help.get: An answer and a prompt to copy. It doesn't start the work.

how.what: Explains how a subsystem works at runtime: the pieces, the flow, where things live, the gotchas.
how.use: Before changing code you don't know. "Where should this live" or "which package owns this".
how.skip: You want the history or the reason (use why). One function you can just read.
how.prompt: /how does the laptop proxy get a request to a dev server on a box?
how.get: Overview, step-by-step flow with file:line, gotchas, and a Mermaid diagram (a berth artifact in Shipyard).

why.what: Finds why something is the way it is, from every source it can reach: git history, tickets, docs, chat, logs, error tracking, analytics.
why.use: Design rationale, "when did this start" regressions, a threshold someone picked, before changing something that looks wrong.
why.prompt: /why does shots compare fall back to turn-start instead of failing?
why.get: A cited answer with confidence tiers, an evidence timeline, and a sources-consulted table.

teach.what: Runs how and why together and weaves them into one plain explanation, built up diagram by diagram.
teach.use: You want to really understand a change or subsystem: onboarding, a big PR you didn't write.
teach.prompt: /teach me how berth notifications get back to the agent that started the work
teach.get: One layered explanation with diagrams you can come back to.

recall.what: Rebuilds your recent context on a topic from your own transcripts, project memory, live state and past fixes.
recall.use: Starting or resuming work. "Where did I leave off on X?"
recall.skip: Catching up on this chat only (use ketchup).
recall.prompt: /recall my work on phone pairing this week
recall.get: A short current-state brief: done, open, decided, next.

ketchup.what: Catches you up on what changed in this chat since your last message.
ketchup.use: After a long background stretch, or when several agents reported while you were away.
ketchup.get: A few plain sentences, each action item with enough context to decide, and an artifact only when there's data or a screen.

in-your-own-words.what: Plays back your goal and the real problem before any work starts.
in-your-own-words.use: A long or messy ask, and you want to check the agent got it before it builds.
in-your-own-words.get: A short restatement you can correct.

sharpen.what: Reframes a task the way a top expert would approach it, aimed at what you're after, without over-specifying.
sharpen.use: Before a big ask you're not sure how to phrase.
sharpen.skip: You already know exactly what you want.
sharpen.prompt: /sharpen I want agents to report back better from worktrees
sharpen.get: The sharpened task, and what it deliberately leaves to you.

bro.what: Restates the last reply in plain words, no jargon.

architect.what: Settles types, signatures and module shape before code, with parallel designs, then stays in the loop while code fills in.
architect.use: Code that crosses a function boundary, a new module or API, or anywhere jumping to code would lock in the wrong shape.
architect.prompt: /architect a notification inbox that survives box restarts
architect.get: Rationale, module map, red flags, and the chosen signatures, at a checkpoint before code.

arena.what: Runs several attempts at the same thing in separate worktrees, picks the best as a base, and grafts in the best parts of the others.
arena.use: Several valid shapes and you can't tell which is best until you see them. A second opinion on an approach.
arena.prompt: /arena take my prompt to the arena verbatim and compare their proposals with yours
arena.get: A runners × criteria table, a diff summary per attempt, and the grafted result.
arena.where: Feature, when the code has several valid shapes

swarm.what: Fans out workers across slices or races, five at a time, and returns one report with a coverage table.
swarm.use: The same check across many packages or pages. Racing hypotheses. Broad exploration.
swarm.prompt: /swarm check every package under internal/ with go vet and its tests. one worker per package. one report.
swarm.get: A coverage table (live in Shipyard) and the combined findings.

interrogate.what: Reviewers on different model families attack a diff from separate angles, then a lead sorts real findings from noise.
interrogate.use: Before shipping a contested design or a risky diff. "Tear this apart."
interrogate.prompt: /interrogate the whole branch, skeptically. no nitpicks unless it's a real bug.
interrogate.get: A findings × reviewers table and a verdict: kept, dismissed, and why.
interrogate.where: Feature step 7 when contested, Opening a PR

blast-radius.what: Finds what a small-looking change could break elsewhere, and proves the one fact it's safe because of by running code.
blast-radius.use: A small diff you don't trust. A change to a shared helper.
blast-radius.prompt: what's the blast radius of making worktreeURL read the proxy port?
blast-radius.get: A risks and cleared table, showing how far each item was proven.

tdd.what: Writes the failing test first, then the fix.
tdd.use: You ask for TDD or a regression test, or the bug has an obvious cheap local test.
tdd.skip: The test path is unclear, slow or integration-heavy.
tdd.get: A red test, the fix, and the green run.

benchmark-checklist.what: Vets a number you measured (what limits it, errors, repeat runs, relevance) before you trust or report it.
benchmark-checklist.use: Any speedup or regression you measured yourself.
benchmark-checklist.get: A chart or table with every run, the spread, the limiter and the source command.

no-comments.what: Strips comments before review. A read-only reviewer flags them, the accepted ones go, and claimed constraints get turned into checks instead.
no-comments.use: Right before a review or PR.
no-comments.get: A diff with only the comments that explain why, plus offers to encode the rest.

unslop.use: PR descriptions, docs, release notes, messages.
unslop.prompt: can we unslop the README changes?

technical-writing.what: A layered standard for docs, RFCs, READMEs, PR descriptions and commits.
technical-writing.use: Writing anything another person reads in order to do something.
technical-writing.prompt: /technical-writing review the Unreleased section of the changelog
technical-writing.get: A rewrite against the standard, with the changes named.

typescript-best-practices.what: Type-system discipline in TypeScript syntax: illegal states unrepresentable, parse at the edges.
typescript-best-practices.use: Loads itself when Claude reads or edits .ts or .tsx files.
typescript-best-practices.get: Stricter types in the code it writes.

show-me-your-work.what: Keeps a decision log for long or unattended work: one row per decision with what, why, evidence and result.
show-me-your-work.use: Overnight runs, multi-phase work, anything you'll review later.
show-me-your-work.prompt: /show-me-your-work keep a decision trail I can review when I'm back
show-me-your-work.get: decisions.tsv, shown live as a table in Shipyard.

figure-it-out.what: Designs a custom, auditable playbook when none of the bundled ones fit.
figure-it-out.use: Big migrations, ambitious multi-part changes, work you'll trust after stepping away.
figure-it-out.skip: A task one playbook already covers.
figure-it-out.prompt: /figure-it-out move every caller from the sync store to the async one, behavior identical
figure-it-out.get: A framing artifact, a hypothesis loop, and a live decision log.

reflect.what: Three reviewers read this chat and turn what was learned into concrete edits to existing skills.
reflect.use: After a long task landed, or one that took too long.
reflect.prompt: /reflect that took too long. capture what we learned.
reflect.get: Proposed skill edits for you to approve.

correct.what: Finds mistakes agents keep repeating and makes each impossible: architecture, then types, then a lint or hook, then a test, docs last.
correct.use: The same correction has landed twice.
correct.get: A rule → enforcer table, each check proven to fail on a real past mistake.

automate-me.what: Drafts your own -mode skill from your transcripts and memory, routing through shipit.
automate-me.use: You want agents to work your way by default.

create-verification-skill.what: Generates a project-local verify skill that drives your app like a user and saves proof a PR can embed.
create-verification-skill.use: A project has no scripted way to prove UI, CLI or service behavior.
create-verification-skill.get: A .claude/skills/verify-<app>/ skill with a feature map.

maintain-verification-skill.what: Keeps the verify skill honest: parallel source readers, one live pass over every feature, at most one PR of proven fixes.
maintain-verification-skill.use: Every so often, or when the verify skill feels stale.
maintain-verification-skill.get: A coverage table per feature and at most one PR.

ideation.name: Ideation
ideation.what: Lays out real options with a recommendation, then stops for your pick. No code, no branch.
ideation.say: "I want to…", "what if we…", "help me plan", "no code"

investigation.name: Investigation
investigation.what: Answers a read-only question (how X works, why Y was built this way) from the code and its history. Changes nothing.
investigation.say: "how does X work", "why was Y built this way", "are we sure", "don't change any code"

research.name: Research
research.what: Scores how other products do X in a matrix with sources, a steal list and a recommendation. No code in your repo.
research.say: "how do other tools do X", "audit competitors"

feature.name: Feature
feature.what: Builds new or changed behavior from a named data shape. Subagents write the code; the lead owns design, review and proof.

bug-fix.name: Bug fix
bug-fix.what: Reproduces a reported defect, finds the root cause, fixes it and proves the fix with runtime evidence.

refactoring.name: Refactoring
refactoring.what: Changes the structure of code while its behavior stays identical.

prototype.name: Prototype
prototype.what: Builds a throwaway sketch to settle a design or behavior question cheaply. The real build follows Feature.
prototype.say: "mock it up", "try a few layouts", "sketch it to decide"

design-audit.name: Design audit
design-audit.what: Audits UI against the design system and iterates until every axis scores 8/10 or better, proven by light and dark screenshots.

visual-parity.name: Visual parity
visual-parity.what: Makes two UIs match pixel for pixel, checked by image diff. The baseline is the spec and is never touched.
visual-parity.say: "match this pixel for pixel", "migrate the styling"

perf-issue.name: Perf issue
perf-issue.what: Traces a measured slowness and improves it against a baseline. Every fix is tied to a measurement.

hillclimb.name: Hillclimb
hillclimb.what: Improves one metric toward a target in a loop: one hypothesis at a time, before and after for each, one commit per accepted win.
hillclimb.say: "keep improving X until it hits Y"

runtime-forensics.name: Runtime forensics
runtime-forensics.what: Diagnoses a live symptom (leak, idle CPU, glitch) by instrumenting the running process. The deliverable is a cited diagnosis, not a fix.
runtime-forensics.say: "memory leak", "idle CPU", "it glitches every few seconds"

trace-forensics.name: Trace forensics
trace-forensics.what: Diagnoses a captured profile, trace or heap snapshot. The deliverable is a diagnosis.

eval.name: Eval
eval.what: Runs a blind experiment to test whether a skill, structure or prompt change helps, before it is promoted.

opening-a-pr.name: Opening a PR
opening-a-pr.what: Opens the PR at the end of every build playbook. Requires the proof pack.
opening-a-pr.say: "open the PR" (also ends every build playbook)

babysit.name: Babysit
babysit.what: Drives a PR to merge-ready (conflicts, review threads, CI) and stops where your call begins.

shipping.name: Shipping
shipping.what: Verifies each green PR independently, then lands only the verified ones.

autonomous-run.name: Autonomous run
autonomous-run.what: Drives a long task to a defined done check without stopping.

session-pickup.name: Session pickup
session-pickup.what: Resumes or takes over another agent's in-flight work from its trail, without redoing it.

pause-safely.name: Pause safely
pause-safely.what: Stops in-flight work cleanly and leaves a checkpoint a fresh agent can resume from.

worktree-cleanup.name: Worktree cleanup
worktree-cleanup.what: Reclaims disk by pruning merged or abandoned worktrees, after checking no live chat still uses them.
